title: Red Engine 2 2D game
description: A `*.game2d.json`: `red_engine2 describe 2d`. Generated by `red_engine2 schema` from src/content/; do not edit.

tables.description: name -> lines of text (`{"pick": table, "by": expr}`).

effects.description: name -> a named group of actions.

pause_if.description: While this expression holds the world stands still but press rules run (a pause menu made of rules).

icon.description: A sprite name: the window, taskbar and shortcut icon.

Capabilities.description: What the game declares it uses (`red_engine2 capabilities`).

View.description: The virtual screen and the camera.

Sprite.description: A sprite: pixel rows (or frames) and a palette.

Score.description: A score: instruments, tracks and the global settings.

title.description: The track's name for people (a pause menu shows it; an exported file is called it).

ScoreTrack.description: One track: an instrument and what it plays.

Prefab.description: A kind of thing in the game.

Move.description: How a thing moves (exactly one mover; the checker says so).

WalkMove.description: Walks along the ground, turning at walls (and ledges).

Backdrop.description: A band of far scenery that scrolls slower than the world.

Widget.description: A HUD widget: flat text, or one kind under its key.

TextSource.description: A text: a template string, or one entry of a string table.

Action.description: An action (one key, or `apply` with its `with`).

At.description: Where: `self`, `other`, `pointer`, `[x, y]`, or a random range `{"x": [min, max], "y": [min, max]}`.

View3d.description: A small 3D scene in a rectangle.

View3dItem.description: A model placed in a view.

Minimap.description: A flat map of the world.

ImageWidget.description: A sprite drawn on the screen.

Trigger.description: A rule's trigger (exactly one; the checker says so).

Model.description: A 3D model: primitives and sprites pressed into voxels.

Layer3d.description: A 3D viewport drawn among the entities.

Step.description: One step (exactly one of the step keys, with `seconds` / `until` / `timeout` beside it).

Reach.description: Map analysis: can a walker reach a place.
